However, a decreased response to war- farin seemed to be caused by ritonavir when it was added to the multidrug therapy of a patient.5 Ritonavir has also been reported to decrease the response to acenocoumarol.6 Up to October 2005 there had been 19 reports7 received by the Canadian health authorities (Health Canada) of enhanced re- sponse to warfarin between 1 and 11 days after starting oseltami- vir. The increased INR ranged from 3.2 to 10.9; however, there was not enough information to be certain of causality. In 3 other cases there was a decrease in INR on the addition of oseltamivir. 1. Bar- biturates, by inducing liver metabolism, can reduce the activity of anticoagulants; glutethimide has a similar action. The benzo- diazepines do not generally have any effect although there is the rare report of increased or decreased activity.
